preamble: In Andalusian Spanish, syllable-final /s/ before /b/ can surface as the voiceless bilabial fricative [ɸ]. Coda /s/ first weakens to an aspiration [h], the aspiration takes on the bilabial place of the following /b/, and the /b/ is devoiced. The result is [hɸ] or a long [ɸː] (/sb/ → [hβ] → [hɸ] → [ɸː]), so in that slot /s/ is realized as [ɸ]. The outcome varies: some descriptions of Eastern Andalusian transcribe the same cluster with a labiodental [fː]. The process is limited to southern Peninsular Spanish and depends on the following consonant, so it is a regional allophone of /s/, not a phonemic change.

examples.note: Coda /s/ assimilates to [ɸ] before /b/ by way of [hβ] > [hɸ] > [ɸː] (Obaid 1973, as summarized on Wikipedia)
Eastern Andalusian; recorded by Rodríguez-Castellano and Palacio (1948), as reviewed by Herrero de Haro (2017)
Salvador (1957) transcribes /sb/ with a labiodental [fː], which shows the outcome varies between [ɸ] and [f]; the same treatment applies across word boundaries

sources: Herrero de Haro, A. (2017). The phonetics and phonology of Eastern Andalusian Spanish: A review of literature from 1881 to 2016. Íkala 22(2), 313–357. https://doi.org/10.17533/udea.ikala.v22n02a09
Obaid, A. H. (1973). The Vagaries of the Spanish "S". Hispania 56(1), 60–67. https://doi.org/10.2307/339038
context: Syllable-final /s/ before /b/ (word-internally and across word boundaries) in Andalusian Spanish
allophones_note: Aspirated coda /s/ takes on the bilabial place of a following /b/, which is devoiced, giving [hɸ] or [ɸː]; [fː] also occurs
